glossary.definition: A JSON document an MCP server publishes that names the server (resource) and the authorization servers that can issue tokens for it. Clients find it from the resource_metadata parameter of the 401 challenge or from a well-known URL.
The header on a 401 or 403 that tells the client how to authenticate: Bearer followed by auth-params such as resource_metadata, scope and error.
A one-time secret (code verifier) whose SHA-256 hash is sent with the authorization request, so a stolen authorization code is useless. MCP clients refuse servers whose metadata does not list S256.
The resource parameter names the MCP server a token is for. The authorization server copies it into the token audience so the server can reject tokens meant for someone else.
The authorization server adds iss=<its issuer> to every authorization response so the client can tell which server answered and detect mix-up attacks.
A client uses an https URL as its client_id; the URL serves a JSON document describing the client. The MCP page says servers and clients SHOULD support it. It is an Internet-Draft, so it can change.
A client registers itself at a registration_endpoint and gets a client_id. The MCP page keeps it for backwards compatibility (MAY).
The token is valid but lacks a scope. The server answers 403 with error="insufficient_scope" and the scope needed, which lets the client step up instead of failing.
A gateway that answers protected resource metadata for any path. A probe then proves the gateway is there, not the application behind it.

sources.title: MCP Authorization (2025-11-25)
sources.use: Whole page: RFC 9728 MUST, discovery order, scope in WWW-Authenticate SHOULD, PKCE and S256, resource parameter MUST (client side), audience validation MUST, 401/403, insufficient_scope 403 SHOULD, CI

sources.title: MCP Authorization (draft)
sources.use: Only the standards list was read: it lists RFC 9207 (the 2025-11-25 page does not mention it). A draft can change.

sources.title: RFC 9728 section 3 (metadata request)
sources.use: Well-known URI construction and the resource value MUST be identical rule (section 3.3).

sources.title: RFC 9728 section 2 (metadata parameters)
sources.use: resource is REQUIRED; authorization_servers is OPTIONAL in the RFC (MCP makes it required).

sources.title: RFC 9728 section 3.3
sources.use: The returned resource MUST be identical to the resource the metadata was requested for, otherwise the data MUST NOT be used.

sources.title: RFC 9728 section 5.1 (WWW-Authenticate resource_metadata)
sources.use: The resource_metadata parameter carries the metadata URL and may be combined with other parameters.

sources.title: RFC 8414 section 3.3 (metadata validation)
sources.use: The issuer value returned MUST be identical to the authorization server identifier used to build the metadata URL. code_challenge_methods_supported is OPTIONAL in the RFC (MCP requires it).

sources.title: RFC 8707 section 2 (resource parameter)
sources.use: The AS SHOULD audience-restrict issued tokens; for an unacceptable resource it should answer invalid_target; it MAY accept a request without resource.

sources.title: RFC 9207 sections 2 and 2.3 (iss parameter)
sources.use: A supporting AS MUST include iss in every authorization response (errors too), equal to its issuer, and MUST set authorization_response_iss_parameter_supported to true.

sources.title: RFC 7636 section 4.2 (code_challenge_method)
sources.use: A client capable of S256 MUST use S256. The RFC does not require a server to advertise methods (that is RFC 8414 plus the MCP page).

sources.title: RFC 6750 section 3 (WWW-Authenticate)
sources.use: A resource server MUST include WWW-Authenticate when no valid token is presented; the Bearer scheme MUST be followed by one or more auth-param values.

sources.title: RFC 9110 challenge grammar
sources.use: Grammar line: challenge = auth-scheme [ 1*SP ( token68 / #auth-param ) ]. Only the grammar line was read.

sources.title: RFC 7591 (initial access token)
sources.use: Definitions section: an initial access token is required when the AS limits the parties that can register; invalid_redirect_uri is a defined error. Rate limiting is not required by the RFC.

sources.title: OAuth Client ID Metadata Document, draft 00
sources.use: Client identifier URLs MUST be https with a path; the document client_id MUST match its URL; the AS SHOULD fetch and SHOULD respect HTTP cache headers. An Internet-Draft: it can change.

sources.title: OpenAI Apps SDK: Authentication
sources.use: Whole page: ChatGPT requires PRM, AS metadata, S256 in code_challenge_methods_supported, echoes resource on authorize and token requests, prefers CIMD, supports DCR, uses RFC 9207 iss to pick a stable

stories.title: An MCP server done right scores 100%
stories.say: A target that follows the MCP authorization page passes every MUST and SHOULD the lab can test.

stories.title: The server: no protected resource metadata
stories.say: Without RFC 9728 metadata a client cannot find the authorization server. The MCP page makes this a MUST.

stories.title: The server: empty first parameter in WWW-Authenticate
stories.say: One stray comma is invalid auth-param syntax. Which real clients choke on it is UNVERIFIED.

stories.title: The server: plain-http metadata URL
stories.say: Metadata that can be rewritten in transit lets an attacker choose the authorization server.

stories.title: The server: S256 not advertised
stories.say: MCP clients must refuse to proceed without S256 advertised; ChatGPT says such servers are unsupported.

stories.title: The server: resource parameter ignored
stories.say: Tokens must be bound to the MCP server they were requested for (RFC 8707).

stories.title: The server: no issuer identification
stories.say: RFC 9207 closes the authorization server mix-up gap; ChatGPT ties its stable redirect URI to it.

stories.title: The server: wrong shape for insufficient scope
stories.say: Without error=insufficient_scope and the needed scope, a client cannot step up.

stories.title: The server: open dynamic registration
stories.say: Open DCR should validate redirect URIs and be gated or throttled. Throttling is a lab heuristic (UNVERIFIED as a requirement).

stories.title: The server: no CIMD support
stories.say: CIMD is the MCP page's default for clients with no prior relationship (SHOULD).

stories.title: The server: stale metadata
stories.say: A lab heuristic (UNVERIFIED as a requirement): stale metadata strands clients on dead endpoints.

stories.title: The server: audience not validated
stories.say: The MCP page makes audience validation a MUST: otherwise tokens can be passed through.

stories.title: A gateway that answers metadata for any path
stories.say: A gateway can answer RFC 9728 metadata for any path, so a probe proves the gateway, not the app behind it.

stories.title: The server: no challenge at all
stories.say: Authorization is optional in MCP, but a server that claims to be protected must challenge.

stories.title: The server: 401 without a scope hint
stories.say: The MCP page says servers SHOULD put scope in the challenge so clients ask for least privilege.

stories.title: The server: metadata names another resource
stories.say: A mismatched resource value is how one server could pose as another.

stories.title: The server: authorization server issuer mismatch
stories.say: RFC 8414 section 3.3: the issuer must be identical, character for character.

stories.title: DCR versus CIMD: what each server offers
stories.say: Per the MCP page CIMD is preferred, DCR is the backwards-compatible fallback, and pre-registration is a third path.

stories.title: 401, then 403 insufficient_scope, then step-up
stories.say: The 403 challenge is the step-up instruction. With the wrong-shape 403 the client is stuck.

stories.title: Step-up fails when the 403 has the wrong shape
stories.say: That is why the lab scores the 403 shape.

stories.title: Probe mode against a local mock only
stories.say: Probe mode is read-only and limited to the one URL typed.

stories.title: Probe refuses private addresses and unsafe targets
stories.say: The probe is a guarded client, not a way into the network behind the SE's laptop.

stories.title: Probe never follows a redirect to another origin
stories.say: The allowlist is the origin typed, and redirects do not widen it.
